key_insight: A fault-tolerant quantum processor can support universal computation using a constant number of external control wires and a fixed, periodically repeated local circuit.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to reducing quantum-chip control wiring and off-chip syndrome traffic, trading control simplicity for execution overhead.
method: Propel quantum information through a planar array using a fixed, clocked, geometrically local depth-3 circuit.
Stream classical instructions through a constant number of external wires, each connected to one qubit.
Prove an accuracy threshold under noisy gates, measurements, and wires, assuming a noiseless global clock.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical threshold theorem, not hardware measurements: n physical qubits support n/polylog(n/ε) logical qubits with error ε per logical gate.
watch_item: The baseline takes n/polylog(n/ε) time per logical gate; faster polylogarithmic timing requires idealized instantaneous, noiseless on-chip classical broadcasts.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
